utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is Case Number IT-02-60/1-A, the Prosecutor versus Momir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [No interpretation] Mr. Nikolic, can you follow the proceedings in a language you can understand? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I can follow the proceedings in a language I understand. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Nikolic. Please be seated. Could I now please ask the parties to identify themselves. Shall we start with the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. The Prosecution is represented by myself, Mathias Marcussen; by Mr. Norman Farrell, senior appeals counsel on the case; and Ms. Lourdes Galicia, who is our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Marcussen. I am now going to turn to the representative of the Defence of Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. LINDSAY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Virginia Lindsay on behalf of Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Ms. Lindsay. Let me remind you that in accordance with the provisions of Rule 65(B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal, a Status Conference must be held within 120 days within the filing of the notice of appeal and then with another 120 days in order to enable to the accused [as interpreted] to raise any issues that he deems important. In this case which is on appeal, this is the third Status Conference. Mr. Nikolic, or Ms. Lindsay, are there any concerns regarding conditions of detention or conditions of health of the accused [as interpreted] that you wish to raise before the Chamber? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't have any particular problems in the Detention Unit. I do have certain problems with my health, but they are being taken care of by the personnel in the Detention Unit and my counsel will advise you of everything that we have discussed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I take note of what you have indicated. You may be seated now. Ms. Lindsay, is there anything that you wish to add to what your defendant has just indicated?

utterances.speaker: MS. LINDSAY
utterances.text: Do you mean in -- I'm not sure if you mean in terms of the conditions of confinement or in general about the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [In English] The condition of the confinement?

utterances.speaker: MS. LINDSAY
utterances.text: No, I have no other issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [In English] Thank you very much. [Interpretation] Let me now turn to the issues regarding the status of this appeal. As for the appeals proceedings, the Appeals Chamber notes that we have so far received all relevant motions in public and confidential versions, including several corrigenda. The Appeals Chamber has also taken note of the amended appeal filed on the 26th of October, 2004. The Appeals Chamber is now considering four motions filed by the parties, including the motion for admission of additional evidence filed by Mr. Nikolic; the motion of Mr. Nikolic asking for judicial notice; motion of the Prosecutor to exclude certain documents including a corrigendum, which has been filed today; and finally, an urgent request filed by Mr. Nikolic today, asking for access to confidential documents filed in the Blaskic [as interpreted] case. As regards the motion submitted by the Prosecution for the purpose of exclusion of certain passages, let me indicate that the filing of this motion was effective on the 24th of November, 2004. The response to this motion is expected not later -- and I emphasise, not later -- 6th of September [as interpreted], 2004. Appeals Chamber will be in a position to render the decision regarding these motions shortly. As far as we are concerned, I do not have that we have any other additional information that needs to be imparted to the Chambers within the framework of this Status Conference. So I will now turn to the parties and ask them if they have any remarks to make or any issues that they wish to raise. Ms. Lindsay, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. LINDSAY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. There's two matters that I would raise. The first is that we do expect to be filing an additional Rule 115 motion. We had hoped to file it by today, but have been unable to do so. We will endeavour to file by the time we file the response to the Prosecution's motion to strike. And we're doing everything we can to file as soon as possible. The other matter that I want to mention is that -- involves a factual error that appeared on the web site of the Tribunal in the part of the web site is in B/C/S. The registry was notified of this error this morning and it's already been corrected, and we wanted to thank them for their rapid response in correcting the error so quickly. However, for quite a long period of time, the web site has indicated that Mr. Nikolic was charged under Article 7(3) in addition to the charges under Article 7(1). Because it was on the web site for so long, I wanted to state publicly for anyone who has seen this that, in fact, Mr. Nikolic has never been charged with command responsibility under Article 7(3) and no such allegations have been made, to my knowledge. Therefore -- I wanted to state that on the record. And other than that I have no other representations to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [In English] Thank you very much, Ms. Lindsay. I took note of the intention that you will shortly you are going to file a motion in the framework of Rule 115, and I am happy that the registry acted accordingly and try to correct the error which was made. So now Mr. Marcussen, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The Prosecution do not have anything to add, any further steps, that we wish to take in the future, other than to respond to filings and things like that. But just maybe to clarify one small matter in relation to what Ms. Lindsay just said. Ms. Lindsay was kind enough to inform us of this issue with the web site this morning and it appears that there might be a discrepancy. I would agree with Ms. Lindsay on this in that in the B/C/S version of the ICTY web site seems to indicate that Mr. Nikolic was charged in the -- what we refer to in these proceedings as the Amended Joinder Indictment from the 27th of May, 2002, on all counts for responsibility under Article 7(3) of the statute. And my learned colleague is correct, that that's not what the indictment -- that that's not how the indictment was phrased. But just a point of clarification is that my colleague said that Mr. Nikolic had not been charged under 7(3) for any crimes, but maybe it wasn't what she meant to say but just for the record Count 6 in the indictment of 27 May 2002 does include a count -- includes responsibility under 7(3). Now, of course, Mr. Nikolic didn't plead guilty to this count when it came up, but I thought I should make it clear that although there is a problem maybe with the web site, it is not entirely -- it's not incorrect for all counts. But I understand that the Registry has corrected this so that the web site will now correspond to the English version of the web site, which I believe has now gotten the facts right. Just this small clarification for Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Marcussen, for the clarification. I believe that the issue is now clear enough unless Ms. Lindsay wishes to add anything. [In English] I see none. [Interpretation] I therefore think that we can adjourn this Status Conference. The Status Conference as adjourned. It is so decided.
